The Democratic and Republican primaries were held on July 19, 2022.{{cite web |title=Voting in Maryland |url=https://elections.maryland.gov/voting/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220715010158/https://elections.maryland.gov/voting/index.html |archive-date=July 15, 2022 |access-date=July 16, 2022 |website=State Board of Elections |publisher=State of Maryland}} Note Archived site contains Primary Election information, but not 'current' version. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Senator [[Chris Van Hollen]] was first elected in [[2016 United States Senate election in Maryland|2016]] with 60.9% of the vote, winning the seat of retiring incumbent [[Barbara Mikulski]]. He ran for a second term against Chris Chaffee, the Republican nominee. Shortly after polls closed on November 8, 2022, the [[Associated Press]] called the race for Van Hollen.{{cite news |title=2022 race calls |url=https://apnews.com/hub/2022-race-calls |access-date=November 8, 2022 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 8, 2022}} He overperformed his 2016 numbers and flipped four counties that he lost in his first election: [[Anne Arundel County, Maryland|Anne Arundel]] (home to the state capital [[Annapolis, Maryland|Annapolis]]), [[Frederick County, Maryland|Frederick]], [[Kent County, Maryland|Kent]], and [[Talbot County, Maryland|Talbot]].
